description: Download a course's files to a folder on the host computer. By default this saves the Content area only, in sub-folders named after the modules. This covers the Content area only, not the whole course. It did not look at: the student's own assignment submissions and instructor feedback (get_assignments, then download_file with folderId and fileId); assignment attachments (get_assignment_files); announcement attachments (get_announcement_files); the syllabus (get_syllabus). TO SAVE MORE IN THE SAME CALL, set everything: true: use it whenever the user asks for the whole course or for everything. It also saves, under the same limits, the student's own assignment submissions, a feedback.md per assignment (score, instructor comments, rubric), the feedback attachments Brightspace lists, the instructor's assignment attachments and announcement attachments. includeSubmissions, includeAssignmentFiles and includeAnnouncementFiles pick them one by one; they cover the whole course even with moduleId. With any of them on, the answer lists only what it still did not look at. The syllabus is never saved by this tool: use get_syllabus for it. Layout: Assignments/<assignment>/feedback.md, my files/ (group assignments: submission files/, naming who submitted), assignment files/, feedback files/ (saved when Brightspace lists them), and Announcements/<date title>/. Existing Content is never moved; a module that would share the extras folder's name is saved under the next free name ("Assignments (2)"), and the answer names the folder used. A rerun skips files already on disk and never overwrites the user's annotated copies. feedback.md is rewritten in place on a rerun when the feedback changed (after grading, say) and the user has not edited it. If they edited it, skip and replace leave it alone and report it; keep_both writes the new text to feedback (2).md and updates that copy from then on (if that copy is edited too, it is left alone and reported). A deleted feedback.md is written again. Use this when the user wants a course (or one module) saved, not download_file once per file. Ask where to save before calling; never guess a directory. Use dryRun first on a large course. The answer counts what was downloaded, skipped, failed and not attempted, and what was not a file (links, embedded videos, broken or locked items): do not report those as missing. If the run stopped (time limit, size limit, file cap, cancel or an expired session) the extra phases may be incomplete or not have run at all, and the answer says so: call it again to continue. If the answer lists anything as unknown or says the course is not fully saved, Brightspace did not answer for it: tell the user exactly which, and never report it as none, empty or not submitted. This tool saves in a folder layout that mirrors the modules; if the student keeps their own layout (they saved with download_file and customFilename), do not use it to pull what is new. To find what is new or missing from the student's saved files ("pull from Brightspace", "what don't I have yet"), call get_unsaved_course_files: it compares the course's content topics by topic id with what download_file and download_course_files saved, then download each listed topic with download_file (topicId). Never conclude a file is absent or not new from get_course_content's modifiedSince: an instructor can upload a file weeks before releasing it, and releasing it does not change its lastModified.

courseId.description: Course ID to download every file from.

downloadPath.description: Absolute path to an existing directory on the HOST filesystem where the course is saved. The directory must already exist; it is not created for you, so create it first if needed. Folders named after the course's modules are created inside it. Ask the user where to save the course before calling this; never guess a directory.

dryRun.description: List the files that would be downloaded without downloading anything or creating any folder. Use it first on a large course.

everything.description: Shorthand that turns on includeSubmissions, includeAssignmentFiles and includeAnnouncementFiles. Use it when the user asks for the whole course or for everything. The syllabus is not included.

existing.description: What to do with a file that is already on disk. skip (default): leave it alone, so running this again only fetches what is new and never overwrites the user's annotated copies. replace: download it again over the old one. keep_both: save the new copy as 'name (1).ext' beside it, unless a copy of the same size is already there.

includeAnnouncementFiles.description: Also save the files attached to announcements, under Announcements/<date title>/. Off by default.

includeAssignmentFiles.description: Also save the instructor's attachments on each assignment, under Assignments/<assignment>/assignment files/. Off by default.

includeSubmissions.description: Also save the student's own submitted files, a feedback.md per assignment (score, instructor comments, rubric) and the feedback attachments Brightspace lists, under Assignments/<assignment>/. Off by default.

maxFiles.description: Most files to download in one call (default 300). Files already on disk do not count. The rest are reported as not attempted: call again to continue, since existing files are skipped.

maxMinutes.description: Wall-clock limit for this call in minutes (default 8). When it passes, the call stops cleanly and reports the rest as not attempted; call it again to continue, since files already on disk are skipped. Raise it only if the client allows long tool calls.

maxTotalMB.description: Most megabytes to download in one call (default 5120, i.e. 5 GB). The rest is reported as not attempted; call again to continue.

moduleId.description: Only download this module and the modules inside it (a module id from get_course_content). Omit to download the whole course.

name: download_course_files
title: Download Course Files
